messages.block1: The platform zakkig (operated by Selim Eser, Dannstadter Straße 6-8, 68199 Mannheim, Germany, hereinafter referred to as “zakkig” or the “Platform Operator”) provides a cloud-based QR code ordering and payment system for the hospitality industry. zakkig enables hospitality establishments (“Merchants” or “Restaurateurs”) to digitally present their menus, automatically route guest orders to kitchen and bar terminals, and process cashless payments via integrated payment service providers. For guests (“Customers” or “Guests”), zakkig enables convenient smartphone-based ordering and payment at the table or for pickup without requiring prior app installation.
messages.block2: Part 1: General Provisions & Scope of Application
messages.block4:
• (1) These General Terms and Conditions (GTC) govern all business relationships between zakkig and Merchants (Part 2) as well as the use of the platform by Guests (Part 3). Part 1 and Part 4 apply equally to all users of the platform.
  • (2) Deviating, conflicting, or supplementary general terms and conditions of the Merchant shall only become part of the contract if and to the extent that zakkig has expressly agreed to their validity in writing.
  • (3) The incorporation of these GTC with respect to Guests takes place as part of the digital ordering process via the scanned QR code or the order link pursuant to Section 305 (2) of the German Civil Code (BGB) (cf. Regional Court of Lübeck [LG Lübeck], case no. 14 S 19/23).
messages.block6:
• Platform: The websites, web applications, and interfaces provided by zakkig under the domains zakkig.com and app.zakkig.com.
  • Merchant (Partner Establishment): A natural or legal person or partnership with legal capacity acting in the exercise of its commercial or independent professional activity as an entrepreneur (Section 14 BGB) that offers food and beverages in the hospitality sector.
  • Guest (Customer): Any natural person ordering food and beverages from a Merchant via the platform as a consumer (Section 13 BGB) or commercial entity.
  • Order: The request initiated by the Guest via the platform for the preparation and provision of food and beverages for on-site consumption (Dine-in) or pickup (Takeaway).
messages.block9:
• (1) Using the platform as a Merchant requires creating a merchant account. Registration is exclusively reserved for entrepreneurs within the meaning of Section 14 BGB. There is no legal entitlement to concluding a user agreement.
  • (2) The Merchant undertakes to provide true, current, and complete information regarding their business and person during registration.
  • (3) The Merchant is obliged to keep login credentials confidential and protect them against unauthorized third-party access. Terminal pairing links may only be shared with authorized operational staff within internal restaurant workflows.
messages.block10: Section 4 Scope of Services provided by zakkig (SaaS Services)
messages.block11:
• (1) zakkig grants the Merchant access to the web-based software solution (Software-as-a-Service) for the contract duration. This includes in particular:

    – The administrative dashboard for managing menus, categories, prices, tax rates, and table configurations;

    – The automated QR code generator for generating table-specific or pickup-specific QR codes and print templates;

    – The digital kitchen display (live order view) and terminal interfaces for real-time order tracking and status management;

    – The 86-availability terminal for rapid deactivation of sold-out items;

    – The order archive and revenue reports for internal operational overview.
  • (2) zakkig provides the technical infrastructure for routing guest orders and the technical integration with payment providers. However, zakkig never becomes a party to the hospitality or purchase contract between Guest and Merchant.
messages.block12: Section 5 Payment Processing and Stripe Connect
messages.block13:
• (1) To receive cashless guest payments, the Merchant is required to maintain a verified Stripe Connect account with Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd. and link it with their zakkig account.
  • (2) Payouts of guest payments are made directly via Stripe to the bank account registered by the Merchant, minus the agreed zakkig platform fee.
  • (3) The Merchant enters into a separate agreement with Stripe regarding payment processing (Stripe Connected Account Agreement). zakkig has no direct access to the Merchant's payout bank account and assumes no liability for payout delays or reserves imposed by Stripe due to regulatory compliance or anti-money-laundering (KYC) reviews.
messages.block15:
• (1) For using the platform, zakkig charges the Merchant a transaction-based platform fee per successful guest order. The specific amount of the platform fee is determined by the pricing overview agreed upon upon contract conclusion.
  • (2) The platform fee is automatically deducted from the gross order amount during the payment process via Stripe Connect and remitted to zakkig.
  • (3) There are no monthly base fees, setup fees, or minimum revenue requirements, unless explicitly agreed otherwise in an individual plan.
messages.block16: Section 7 Obligations and Responsibilities of the Merchant
messages.block17:
• (1) Pricing and Tax Rates: The Merchant is solely responsible for ensuring that all prices listed in their menu are final gross prices inclusive of applicable value-added tax (VAT) and that the correct tax rates (e.g. 7% or 19% VAT) are configured.
  • (2) Food Information Regulations (FIC / LMIV): The Merchant is legally obligated to independently, accurately, and up-to-date provide all mandatory declarations pursuant to the Food Information to Consumers Regulation (EU Regulation 1169/2011 - FIC / LMIV) for each item, including allergen declarations, additives, and alcohol content.
  • (3) Protection of Minors: The Merchant must ensure that all statutory provisions on youth protection (e.g. German Youth Protection Act - JuSchG) are strictly observed upon handing over alcoholic beverages.
  • (4) Lawful Content: The Merchant warrants that all uploaded texts, pictures, and logos do not infringe any third-party copyrights, trademark rights, or personal rights.
  • (5) Cash Register Regulations & Taxes (GoBD / TSE): zakkig is strictly an ordering and payment processing system and does not constitute a certified electronic recording system with a certified technical security device (TSE) pursuant to Section 146a of the German Fiscal Code (AO / KassenSichV). The Merchant is solely responsible for properly recording revenues in their own point-of-sale or accounting system, declaring taxes, and complying with statutory receipt issuance obligations.
messages.block18: Section 8 Availability, Maintenance, and Service Disruptions
messages.block19:
• (1) zakkig strives to maintain an annual platform availability of 98.5% on average. This excludes scheduled maintenance windows and downtimes attributable to force majeure or circumstances outside zakkig's reasonable control (e.g. internet backbone outages, disruptions of Cloudflare, Convex, or Stripe).
  • (2) Scheduled maintenance is conducted during periods of low platform usage (e.g. nighttime) whenever feasible.
messages.block21:
• (1) The user agreement between zakkig and the Merchant is concluded for an indefinite period. Unless a minimum contract term has been agreed, the agreement may be terminated by either party at any time to the end of the current calendar month in text form (e.g. via email).
  • (2) The right to extraordinary termination for good cause remains unaffected. Good cause for zakkig exists in particular if the Merchant materially breaches their obligations under Section 7 or if abusive or fraudulent transactions are processed via their account.
  • (3) Upon the effective date of termination, access to the merchant dashboard is deactivated. The Merchant must independently export and archive their operational data and reports prior to contract end.
messages.block23: To the extent that zakkig processes personal data of guests on behalf of the Merchant in the course of providing services, the parties enter into a separate Data Processing Agreement (DPA) pursuant to Article 28 GDPR that complies with statutory legal requirements.
messages.block24: Part 3: Specific Provisions for Guests / Consumers (B2C)
messages.block25: Section 11 Role of zakkig as Technical Intermediary
messages.block26:
• (1) zakkig provides guests with a technical platform to inspect menus of participating restaurants, select food and beverage items, and make cashless payments.
  • (2) Contracting Parties: The hospitality, catering, or sales contract regarding the preparation, delivery, and transfer of food and beverages is concluded exclusively and directly between the Guest and the respective Merchant.
  • (3) zakkig does not become a party to this hospitality contract, is not the seller of the food, and assumes no warranty or liability for the condition, freshness, temperature, allergen compliance, or overall quality of the prepared food and beverages.
messages.block27: Section 12 Ordering Process and Formation of Contract
messages.block28:
• (1) The presentation of food and beverages in the digital menu does not constitute a legally binding offer by the Merchant, but an invitation to place an order (invitatio ad offerendum).
  • (2) By completing the checkout and payment process, the Guest submits a legally binding offer to conclude a contract with the Merchant for the items in the shopping cart.
  • (3) The contract between Guest and Merchant is concluded as soon as payment is confirmed and the order is routed to the establishment's kitchen system, which is signaled to the Guest by the display of the order confirmation and order number.
messages.block30:
• (1) Payment is conducted via the integrated payment service provider Stripe using the payment methods offered (e.g. credit card, debit card, Apple Pay, Google Pay).
  • (2) Upon successful charge of the selected payment method, the Guest's payment obligation toward the Merchant is discharged with debt-discharging effect (schuldbefreiende Wirkung).
messages.block31: Section 14 Statutory Exclusion of the Right of Withdrawal
messages.block32:
• (1) Pursuant to Section 312g (2) No. 1 BGB, consumers have no right of withdrawal for contracts for the supply of goods that are liable to deteriorate or expire rapidly (this applies to freshly prepared food and beverages).
  • (2) Furthermore, pursuant to Section 312g (2) No. 9 BGB, there is no right of withdrawal for contracts for the provision of services in connection with leisure activities and catering if the contract provides for a specific date or period of performance.
messages.block34: All complaints and inquiries regarding ordered food and beverages (e.g. defects, incomplete delivery, incorrect items, delays, intolerances) must be addressed directly to the on-site restaurant management. As the sole contractual partner, the Merchant is responsible for fulfilling any statutory warranty claims.

  • (4) The foregoing limitations of liability also apply mutatis mutandis in favor of the legal representatives, employees, and vicarious agents of zakkig. Mandatory liability under the German Product Liability Act (ProdHaftG) remains unaffected.
